page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features a cache hierarchy consisting of a 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance profiles across multiple compute and memory operations. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and bfloat16 operations. In synthetic testing, the server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 66,066.16 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 47,820.44. Memory performance is highlighted by a cached read-only small-block bandwidth of 3,532.24 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidths return to average tiers at 173.98 GB/sec and 68.56 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression reach top-tier performance levels, registering 36.1 GB/sec and 15.17 GB/sec.

With its high-frequency Intel Xeon processor and specialized instruction sets, the D48ls_v7 is optimized for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, scoring 22,291.38 on PassMark database tests, and handles Redis SET operations at 79.02 million operations per second. The hardware is also capable of handling lightweight machine learning tasks, processing 135M parameter LLM text generation at a top-tier 331.81 tokens per second, though performance drops to average levels for larger 70B models. The lack of local storage and a relatively low memory-to-vCPU ratio represent key tradeoffs, making this instance best suited for compute-intensive tasks, web serving, and cryptographic processing rather than memory-bound databases or local storage-heavy applications.
